correctness.rationale: D has trivial kernel; its Gram matrix has the binomial Toeplitz form. An explicit nonintersecting path family establishes positivity of every complementary minor of the sign-conjugate Gram matrix, so the inverse Gram kernel is entrywise strictly positive. The exact remainder is the Hilbert orthogonal projection identity plus the exact unimodular phase-graph identity; the sharp binomial normalization and Landau example were verified against Hindov et al. Rational finite Gram tests and 640 deterministic complex examples agree. The phase bound follows from a complete-graph identity. No computational finite test is treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The newly sharp finite-support Sobolev endpoint lacked an explicit robust all-complex equality description. An entrywise positive Green matrix exists at every order, so the deficit is an exact sum of independently interpretable phase and amplitude energies, characterizes all equality cases and gives computable quantitative near-equality control; this is structural stability information rather than merely a new constant, a renamed inequality, or a single finite example. The coefficient is deliberately not claimed optimal.
